title: 半波整流 + 电容滤波：把交流变成直流
summary: 信号发生器 → 二极管 → 1 kΩ 负载，只剩正半周。按住按键并上 100 µF 电容：输出变成一条带纹波的直流。用示波器的平均值和峰峰值看清楚。
concepts: 二极管：单向导通 diode as a one-way valve
平均值 = 直流分量 average = DC component
电容滤波与纹波 capacitor filter and ripple
非正弦周期波 non-sinusoidal periodic wave
description: 信号发生器（正弦波 50 Hz、幅度 5 V）→ D1（硅二极管，0.65 V + 0.8 Ω）→ VOUT → R1（1 kΩ）→ GND；按键 SW1 把 C1（100 µF）并在 VOUT 和 GND 之间。CH1 看输入，CH2 看 VOUT。整流后的波形 = 直流 + 各次谐波；电容留下直流，压小纹波。

cards.title: 负半周去哪了？
text: 信号发生器和两支探头已经在板上。**二极管**：有黑圈（负极）的一头朝右，**`b3`**–**`b8`**。**电阻**（`1 kΩ`）**`c8`**–**`tn8`**。
信号发生器：**正弦波、`50 Hz`、幅度 `5 V`**（和市电同一个频率）。CH1 看输入，CH2 看电阻上的电压 VOUT。
CH1 有上半周也有下半周。CH2 呢？

cards.title: 单向阀和水桶
text: - **二极管**是一个单向阀：正极比负极高出约 0.65 V，它才导通；反过来就断开。所以只有正半周能过去，输出是一串“小山包”——这叫**半波整流**。
- 这串小山包不是正弦波，但它有一个**平均值**——这就是它的直流成分，万用表直流档读到的就是它。剩下的起伏是各种频率的交流成分。
- 想要平稳的直流，就并一个大电容当**水桶**：每到波峰，二极管把桶灌满；两次波峰之间，负载慢慢从桶里取电，电压只往下掉一点。掉的那一点叫**纹波**。
![](fig:waves)
- 两次波峰之间隔一个周期 1/f，这段时间里电容放掉的电荷约是 I/f，所以
其中 I ≈ 输出电压 ÷ 1 kΩ。动手之前先估一估。
![](fig:circuit)

cards.title: 按下按键，接上水桶
text: - **松开按键**：读 CH2 的「平均」。
- **点一下按键**让它保持按下：等波形稳定，读 CH2 的「平均」和 **Vpp**（纹波）。这时把 CH2 的伏/格调小，纹波看得更清楚。

cards.title: 带走
text: - 整流后的波形 = **直流 + 一串谐波**（频率是 50 Hz 整数倍的正弦波）。平均值就是直流成分；电容（低通）留下直流，把谐波压小。
- 纹波 $ΔV ≈ I / (fC)$：负载电流越大、电容越小，纹波越大。全波整流的波峰间隔减半，纹波也减半。
- 坑：100 µF 是**电解电容**，+ 脚接二极管负极那一侧（VOUT），− 脚接 GND。接反会发热、鼓包甚至爆开。仿真里的电容不分正负。
- 坑：千万不要直接拿市电做这个实验。真实电源先用变压器降压、隔离，再整流滤波——变压器在理论题里练。
- 选学：非正弦波怎么拆成谐波（傅里叶）、怎样用拉普拉斯变换解暂态、怎样把一级电路看成一个二端口——各章的要点从下面进入。

caption.text: 输入（虚线）；没有电容时只剩一串正半周的小山包；接上电容，输出在波峰被充满，两次波峰之间慢慢下降——下降的那一点就是纹波（图里画得夸张了）。

i18n.en: The input (dashed); without the capacitor only the positive humps are left; with it, the output is topped up at each peak and sags a little in between — that sag is the ripple (exaggerated here).

caption.text: 二极管只让电流从左往右流；按住按键（S1 闭合），C1（彩色）就并在负载 R1 旁边当“水桶”。

i18n.en: The diode only lets current flow left to right; hold the button (S1 closed) and C1 (in colour) sits beside the load R1 as a "bucket".

en.title: Half-wave rectifier + capacitor filter: from AC to DC
en.summary: Generator → diode → 1 kΩ load: only the positive half survives. Hold a button to add 100 µF: the output becomes DC with a little ripple. The scope's average and peak-to-peak show it clearly.
concepts: the diode as a one-way valve
en.description: Generator (sine 50 Hz, amplitude 5 V) → D1 (silicon diode, 0.65 V + 0.8 Ω) → VOUT → R1 (1 kΩ) → GND; button SW1 puts C1 (100 µF) between VOUT and GND. CH1 on the input, CH2 on VOUT. The rectified wave is DC plus harmonics; the capacitor keeps the DC and shrinks the ripple.

cards.title: Where did the negative half go?
text: The generator and both probes are already on the board. **Diode**: the end with the band (the cathode) faces right, **`b3`**–**`b8`**. **Resistor** (`1 kΩ`) **`c8`**–**`tn8`**.
Generator: **sine, `50 Hz`, amplitude `5 V`** (the mains frequency). CH1 shows the input, CH2 the voltage VOUT across the resistor.
CH1 has a top half and a bottom half. What about CH2?

cards.title: A one-way valve and a bucket
text: - A **diode** is a one-way valve: it conducts only when its anode is about 0.65 V above its cathode, and blocks the other way. So only the positive halves get through and the output is a row of humps — **half-wave rectification**.
- These humps are not a sine wave, but they have an **average** — their DC part, which is what a multimeter's DC range reads. The rest of the wobble is AC at various frequencies.

- For a steady DC, add a big capacitor as a **bucket**: at every peak the diode fills it up; between peaks the load slowly draws from it, and the voltage only sags a little. That sag is the **ripple**.
![](fig:waves)
- The peaks are one period 1/f apart, and in that time the capacitor gives away a charge of about I/f, so
with I ≈ the output voltage ÷ 1 kΩ. Estimate it before you measure.
![](fig:circuit)

cards.title: Press the button: add the bucket
text: - **Push button** at **`e8`** (straddling the gap): pressed, it joins column `8` to column `10`. **Capacitor** (`100 µF`) into **`c10`**–**`tn10`**.
- **Button released**: read CH2's "Vavg".
- **Click the button** so it stays pressed. Once the trace settles, read CH2's "Vavg" and its **Vpp** (the ripple). Turn CH2's V/div down to see the ripple better.

cards.title: Take away
text: - A rectified wave = **DC + a series of harmonics** (sine waves at whole multiples of 50 Hz). The average is the DC part; the capacitor (a low-pass) keeps the DC and shrinks the harmonics.
- Ripple $ΔV ≈ I / (fC)$: more load current or less capacitance means more ripple. A full-wave rectifier halves the time between peaks, and the ripple with it.
- Pitfall: 100 µF is an **electrolytic**. Its + lead goes to the diode's cathode side (VOUT), its − lead to GND. Reversed, it heats up, bulges or even bursts. The simulated capacitor has no polarity.
- Pitfall: never try this straight on the mains. A real supply first steps the voltage down and isolates it with a transformer, then rectifies and filters — transformers are in the theory problems.
- Electives: how a non-sinusoidal wave splits into harmonics (Fourier), how the Laplace transform solves transients, how to treat a stage as a two-port — each chapter's key points open below.

measurements.explain: Each hump peaks at about 5 × 1000/1050.8 − 0.65 ≈ 4.1 V (the generator's internal 50 Ω takes a little, the diode holds back 0.65 V). The average over a period is a little below 4.1/π ≈ 1.3 V: the input must first pass 0.65 V before the diode conducts, which trims both sides of each hump.

The output moves between about 2.95 V and 3.45 V and averages about 3.2 V. The peaks no longer reach 4.1 V: the capacitor charges only in a short moment near each peak, with a large current, and the generator's internal 50 Ω drops part of the voltage.

I ≈ 3.2 V / 1 kΩ = 3.2 mA, ΔV ≈ I/(fC) = 0.0032 / (50 × 100 µF) ≈ 0.64 V. The reading, about 0.5 V, is smaller: the capacitor does not discharge for a whole period — near each peak the diode is still charging it.

measurements.ask: If the load changes from 1 kΩ to 470 Ω, the ripple will:
choices: Grow: the load drains the bucket faster
Shrink: a smaller resistor drops less voltage
Stay the same: only the capacitor sets the ripple
measurements.explain: ΔV ≈ I/(fC): the resistance drops by more than half, the current more than doubles, and the capacitor gives away more than twice the charge between peaks.

hints: The diode's cathode (the end with the band) faces VOUT (column 8); its anode goes to the generator's column.
The button straddles the gap at e8: column 8 is one end, column 10 the other; the capacitor runs from column 10 to GND.
The scope table's "Vavg" is what a multimeter's DC range would read.
tests: Button released: only the positive halves
compare: - **No capacitor**: only the positive halves are left. Peak ≈ 5 × 1000/1050.8 − 0.65 ≈ 4.1 V; average ≈ 1.22 V, a little below 4.1/π (the diode waits until the input passes 0.65 V).

- **With 100 µF**: the output moves between about 2.95 and 3.45 V, averaging ≈ 3.2 V, with ≈ 0.5 Vpp of ripple. The rough ΔV ≈ I/(fC) = 3.2 mA / (50 Hz × 100 µF) ≈ 0.64 V comes out a little high, because the capacitor does not discharge for a whole period.

- **Why the peaks dropped**: the capacitor charges only in a short moment near each peak, in sharp pulses of tens of milliamps, which drop a few tenths of a volt across the generator's internal 50 Ω. In a real supply the transformer's winding resistance does the same.

tests.name: 按下按键：带纹波的直流

compare: - **没有电容**：只剩正半周。峰值 ≈ 5 × 1000/1050.8 − 0.65 ≈ 4.1 V；平均 ≈ 1.22 V，比 4.1/π 略小（二极管要等输入过了 0.65 V 才导通）。
- **接上 100 µF**：输出在约 2.95～3.45 V 之间，平均 ≈ 3.2 V，纹波 ≈ 0.5 Vpp。粗估 ΔV ≈ I/(fC) = 3.2 mA / (50 Hz × 100 µF) ≈ 0.64 V 偏大一些，因为电容并不是放电整整一个周期。
- **波峰为什么降低了**：电容只在波峰附近短短一段时间里充电，充电电流是几十毫安的尖脉冲，在信号发生器内部 50 Ω 上压掉零点几伏。真实电源里的变压器绕组电阻也有同样的效果。

measurements.explain: 每个山包的峰值约 5 × 1000/1050.8 − 0.65 ≈ 4.1 V（信号发生器内部 50 Ω 分走一点，二极管再拦住 0.65 V）。整个周期的平均比 4.1/π ≈ 1.3 V 还小一点：输入要先超过 0.65 V 二极管才导通，山包两边被削掉了一些。

measurements.ask: 按住按键：CH2 的「平均」（直流输出）
measurements.explain: 输出在约 2.95 V 到 3.45 V 之间，平均约 3.2 V。波峰没有到 4.1 V：电容每次只在波峰附近很短的时间里充电，充电电流很大，在信号发生器内部的 50 Ω 上压掉了一部分。

measurements.ask: 按住按键：CH2 的 Vpp（纹波）
measurements.explain: I ≈ 3.2 V / 1 kΩ = 3.2 mA，ΔV ≈ I/(fC) = 0.0032 / (50 × 100 µF) ≈ 0.64 V。实测约 0.5 V，比估计小：电容并不是整整一个周期都在放电，波峰附近二极管还在给它充电。

choices: 纹波变大：负载取电更快，桶里的水掉得更多
纹波变小：电阻小了，压降小了
不变：纹波只由电容决定
measurements.ask: 如果把负载从 1 kΩ 换成 470 Ω，纹波会？
measurements.explain: ΔV ≈ I/(fC)：电阻小了一半多，电流大了一倍多，两次波峰之间电容放掉的电荷也多一倍多。

hints: 二极管的负极（有黑圈的一头）朝 VOUT（第 8 列），正极接信号发生器那一列。
按键横跨凹槽放在 e8：第 8 列是一端，第 10 列是另一端；电容从第 10 列接到 GND。
示波器表格里的「平均」就是万用表直流档的读数。
